speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether the Government will consider more severe penalties and longer jail sentences for criminals involved in scams using the impersonation of Ministries and Government agencies including those who allow the use of their bank accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have hence focused on punishing and deterring those in Singapore who facilitate scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have also worked with the Inter-agency Sentencing Advisory Panel to publish sentencing guidelines for certain scams related offences last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The guidelines recommend that significant imprisonment terms should be the norm for scam related offences.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In view of the recent reports of scam victims themselves who become involved in carrying out the scams, what would be the sentencing considerations, and if it can be made clear that such victims would not face any leniency under the law?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But I would say that there might be other cases which may contain mitigating factors.
